Figure 1:Cross-magnification provenance verification
in a whole-slide pathology image.(a) The reference context shows the claimed location (red),
ground-truth source (green), and ZoomTrace prediction
(blue dashed).
(b) The returned high-magnification observation originates
from the true source rather than the claimed location.
(c) The claimed and actual source regions exhibit visually
similar tissue structures.
ZoomTrace independently recovers the source
(IoU = 0.998) and correctly identifies the provenance mismatch.

Figure 2:Claim-independent source estimation and verification in ZoomTrace.(a) The query is resampled to the context’s physical resolution;
frozen UNI features retrieve candidate windows, and LoFTR with
RANSAC refines the source estimateB^\widehat{B}.
(b) Reliabilityrrmeasures the winning match’s margin over its
strongest spatially disjoint retrieved competitor. Windows overlapping
the winner are excluded from the rival set.
(c) Only then is the claimℓ\ellintroduced. Reliability thresholdτ\tauand spatial toleranceδ\deltadetermine whether it is verified,
mismatched, or unverifiable.
The tissue comes from Figure1; candidate windows
are schematic placements on the retrieval grid.
